title: Handoff entropy debugging scratchpad
content:
Context:
- Intermittent client-facing latency spikes and a handful of 504s last week during AZ flaps. Not strong enough to be a full outage, but saw unusual handoff churn between regional pools (us-east-1a -> us-east-1b -> us-east-1a) within single user sessions.
- Hypothesis: handoff selector entropy + short TTL on route-cached keys => repeated cold KV-cache warmups causing tokens to spike and some requests to miss SLO.

What I observed (raw breadcrumbs):
- 2026-02-25 03:12 UTC: spike in p95 from 210ms -> 780ms (10m window), error rate 0.7% 504s. Traces show majority of slow requests had handoff=true in headers.
- Traces: x-redwood-routing: {policy:prefer-region, picked_pool:us-east-1b, fallback_pool:us-east-1a, handoff_attempts:2}
- Application logs (snippet):
  [2026-02-25T03:12:17Z] req=abc123 route=chat-v2 handoff=1 selected=us-east-1b kv_cache_miss=true warmup_ms=320
  [2026-02-25T03:12:17Z] req=abc123 attempt=2 selected=us-east-1a kv_cache_miss=true warmup_ms=290
- KV cache size on us-east-1b small at moment of spike (evictions high). Noted concurrent kernel preemption on some hosts (dmesg logs show gpu watchdog soft-ops).

Commands I ran / artifacts I checked (notes + outputs):
- kubectl (on platform infra cluster)
  kubectl logs -n redwood serving-runtime-guard-7f8 -c router | grep abc123  # saw the handoff headers above

- curl to routing policy evaluation endpoint (local dev):
  curl -s -X POST http://localhost:9000/eval -d '{"region":"us-east-1","policy":"prefer-region","session_id":"abc123"}' | jq .   # returned pick: us-east-1b, score:0.82, rand:0.47

- redis-cli info (chain of route-caches)
  # us-east-1b: connected_clients:42, used_memory_human: 1.1G, evicted_keys: 12984, keyspace_hits: 11254, misses: 2041

- curl to model pool health endpoints:
  curl -s https://pool-us-east-1b.internal/health | head -n1 -> {"status":"ok","workers":12,"pending":18}
  curl -s https://pool-us-east-1a.internal/health | head -n1 -> {"status":"ok","workers":16,"pending":3}

- Observed bump in worker pending queues on pool us-east-1b right when handoffs started.

Error snippets copied from router logs: (redacted)
- ERROR route-handoff: failed to allocate transient-kvspace: insufficient-memory (code=OOM_KV)
- WARN policy-eval: tie-breaker entropy increased beyond threshold -> randomized selection used
- INFO handoff: attempt=1 dest=us-east-1b reason=policy-weight-threshold-exceeded retry_delay=120ms

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Entropy-induced oscillation: tie-breakers when pools have similar policy scores cause stochastic picks; with small routing-ttl, subsequent requests in same session can be routed to different pools which each incur KV cold-starts => latency spike.
2) Backpressure mismatch: some pools (1b) are experiencing queueing; policy detects this and sometimes prefers local but fallbacks are noisy -> retries/handoffs exacerbate load.
3) KV cache eviction pressure on smaller pools causing repeated warmups after handoff; eviction threshold tuned too aggressively.
4) Sticky session affinity not honored for multi-attempt flows (edge handshake loses session tag), so handoff attempts don't carry cache hints.

Experiments to try (quick ideas):
- Short term rollback: increase routing-ttl for session keys from 30s -> 300s for chat flows to test reduction in pool oscillation.
  Commands:
    # update local policy (dev only)
    PUT /api/policies/chat-v2 {"routing_ttl_s":300}

- A/B test: disable randomized tie-breaker for prefer-region policy (force deterministic pick by weight) for one hour to observe p95.
- Increase KV cache size on pools flagged with high evictions (us-east-1b) and monitor eviction_rate.
- Add a session-affinity header propagation test to ensure handoff carries cache-hint: set X-Session-KV: true and verify in pool logs.

Notes on instrumentation gaps:
- Router traces include 'rand' but not seed; need persistent seed in traces to correlate selections across attempts.
- No current metric that measures "session-level pool-switches per 5m" — would be valuable.
- KV warmup time currently only logged as 'warmup_ms' in debug; should be aggregated to show p95 warmup per pool.

Short term mitigation plan (if we see immediate reoccurrence):
- Increase routing_ttl for high-traffic chat routes to 2m, pin on-host KV cache increase + alert on eviction_rate > 1000/min.
- Temporarily bias prefer-region policy weight +10% for pools with low pending queue.

Things to watch (dashboard queries):
- rate( router.handoff.count[5m] ) broken down by dest_pool
- p95( request.latency ) filter handoff=true and by selected_pool
- redis.evictions per pool
- worker.pending queue length per pool

Open questions / TODOs:
- Is there any cross-region KV replication for route keys? (I think no — only local per-pool caches.)
- If we bias policy to favor pools with lower pending, do we risk overloading the 'healthy' pool? Need canary config.
- Ask SRE to check for kernel preemption reports on the hosts in us-east-1b during the window.

Immediate next steps (my plan):
- 2026-03-10: create a short-lived policy change in staging to increase session TTL for chat-v2 and run for 6 hours. (PR: GH#4127)
- Add a Grafana panel showing session-level pool-switches (metric design doc: CON-2038)
- Sync with Ethan and Sofia: share these scratch notes + meet Wed 10:00 to run controlled replay.

Random scribbles / helpful commands to reproduce locally:
- produce a high-entropy policy decision trace:
  python tests/route_sim.py --policy prefer-region --seed 42 --clients 200 --pools us-east-1a,us-east-1b

- force handoff from router container:
  echo '{"req_id":"scratch","route":"chat-v2","session":"sess-42"}' | nc -q 1 router.internal 12345

End of scratchpad.

-- Priya D.
